reason:
All 20 targeted syncs succeeded: ten each with uv 0.12.24 and installed uv 0.13.5, using Git 2.56.0 and Python 3.14.9 on Ubuntu 24.04.5 x86_64. The fixture contained three subdirectory packages from one repository, sharing a tag and locked commit. Commands used UV_CACHE_DIR=<temporary-cache> uv sync --frozen --python <python3.14>, with maintenance.auto=false and gc.auto=0. Variants covered local-file and HTTP repositories, cold caches, prolonged initialization, and simultaneous uv processes sharing an initially empty cache. Every invocation installed all three packages; traces showed lock contention without rev-parse overlapping git init, even when initialization exceeded 400 ms.

Related coverage: crates/uv/tests/pip_compile/pip_compile.rs::compile_git_concurrent_access snapshots successful resolution of two subdirectory packages from one pinned GitHub repository. crates/uv/tests/sync/sync.rs::sync_git_repeated_member_backwards_path snapshots installation of two same-repository packages after locking; it does not test cold-cache frozen sync.

This does not rule out the intermittent report. Further reproduction needs the exact project and lockfile, sanitized failing traces with process IDs and lock events, and CI/cache-sharing details. Ubuntu 26.04 and the original GitHub HTTPS repository were not tested. Updated $RUNNER_TEMP/issue-context/README.md with findings and artifact locations.
